inputs.base_revenue_note: TTM to 30 Jun 2026 = FY2025 4,429,452 + H1 2026 2,321,667 - H1 2025 2,116,437 (JPY millions). The TTM base matches the June-2026 balance-sheet anchors so H1 2026 cash generation is not counted twice (once in cash, once in a projected FY2026).
inputs.share_count_basis: Issued 1,334,037,042 less treasury 89,390,759 at 30 Jun 2026 (H1 2026 tanshin, post 2-for-1 split of 1 Jan 2026) = 1,244,646,283. Restricted-stock awards outstanding are tens of thousands of shares, so basic ~= fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and buybacks (JPY 300bn FY2025, JPY 109bn H1 2026) are the mechanism that keeps the count flat, so they are value-neutral here.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 Jun 2026: bonds and borrowings 78,327 current + 481,739 non-current = 560,066; cash and cash equivalents 791,733; net cash 231,667. Lease liabilities (70,086 + 269,662 = 339,748) are EXCLUDED because leases are charged as an operating cost in the flows (treatment B).
inputs.fcf_note: reported_fcf is TTM OCF - PP&E - intangibles = 723,144 - 291,153 (FY2025 373,287 + H1 2026 194,514 - H1 2025 135,810). last_fcf = reported_fcf - lease principal repaid (TTM 74,647) - SBC (1,389) - interest income (15,083) = 340,872. Lease interest (FY2025 11,237) and borrowing interest are already inside OCF. TTM FCF is flattered by a JPY 79bn FY2025 inventory release; the projection is built from components, not from this figure.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Securities Report, consolidated statement of changes in equity, 'Share-based payment' 501 (parent) and cash-flow-statement share-based comp 1,389 (CSV StockBasedComp FY2025). Restricted-stock plan only; no cash-settled equity-award taxes disclosed. Effectively an SBC-zero filer: house and street bases coincide.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income (Note to finance income) 15,083; finance income total 18,165 incl. ~3bn dividends. Stripped from the owner-FCF anchor; cash is in the bridge at face and the equity-instrument portfolio is in equity_bridge at fair value (matching-asset rule).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchase of treasury stock 300,007 (cash-flow statement); H1 2026 a further 109,280. 93,359,400 treasury shares cancelled 23 Jan 2026. Repurchaser: the flat count is funded.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows: 10y JGB ~1.7%, ERP 5.5-6%, beta ~1.0 gives a cost of equity of 7.2-7.7%; after-tax cost of debt ~1.1% on ~10% debt weight (bonds/borrowings 560bn vs ~5.0tn market cap, leases excluded under treatment B) gives a mechanical WACC of ~6.6-7.0%. Used 7.5%: above the mechanical JPY figure because 86% of revenue and most of the economic flows are USD/EUR/other that are merely translated into JPY, below the ~9% house reference for small-cap keiretsu suppliers because Bridgestone is a net-cash global oligopoly leader with no customer concentration. Same WACC in all three scenarios; cyclicality and the China/tariff risks are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B (leases as operating cost): full lease cash cost (principal 74.6bn TTM + interest 11.2bn FY2025 = ~1.86% of revenue) is deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (339.7bn) are excluded from net debt; D&A for the tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A 353,229 less ROU depreciation 70,381 = 282,848; TTM ~289.5bn = 6.25% of revenue). The CSV EBITDA (op income + total D&A) is the IFRS-16 pre-lease figure, which is why the ebitda_margin_path is stated pre-lease.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (NCI profit share ~7.6bn FY2025, ~2% of attributable profit); non-controlling interests of 57,180 (30 Jun 2026) are deducted once in equity_bridge. Not folded into the tax rate.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, routed via dcf-methods as an operating company (non-US, cyclical, IFRS-16 leases, NCI -> owner-fcf-adaptations applied). FY0 is the TTM to June 2026 so that revenue, margins, D&A, capex and the balance sheet all share one date. Margin basis: the EBITDA path is anchored to ADJUSTED operating profit (company definition, excludes business/plant restructuring expenses of 94bn in FY2025 and 43bn in FY2024) LESS a ~0.4-0.5pp/yr allowance for the restructuring that has recurred every year since 2020 -- the base-case EBIT settles at 11.5%, i.e. the FY2026 guided 11.4% adjusted margin held roughly flat, not the 13% mid-term-plan target (missed) and not the 11.7% FY2022 pre-tariff peak. Cash tax 28% on EBIT (FY2025 ex the 70.4bn uncertain-tax-position reversal was 28.5%; FY2024 30.7%; Japan statutory ~30.6%, blended group lower). Working capital: a manufacturer with receivables + inventories well above payables (~19% of revenue), so growth consumes cash: wc_capture -15% of the revenue change. Capex is cash PP&E + intangibles (6.3% of TTM revenue; FY2026 plan 410bn less ~75bn ROU additions = ~335bn, 7.2%) and converges to D&A ex-ROU plus a small growth margin. SBC is 0.03% of revenue, so band_position is null: house and street coincide. Price is the regular TSE close, not an after-hours print.

equity_bridge.item: Equity instruments (FVOCI cross-shareholdings in business partners) at fair value
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 Annual Securities Report note 11, 31 Dec 2025. Matching asset for the dividend income excluded from the flows.
H1 2026 balance sheet, 30 Jun 2026. Flows are consolidated, so the NCI claim is deducted once here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: revenue 3yr CAGR (FY2022-25, 2.5%) and constant-currency growth of ~1-2%; the equity CAGR is rejected as a growth proxy
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 11.2% vs revenue 8.2% (37% apart) and 3yr 7.3% vs 2.5%: book value grew on retained earnings and JPY-weakness translation gains, not on operating growth, so it is NOT used. Revenue 5yr CAGR is also FX-inflated (USD/JPY ~107 in FY2020 to ~150 in FY2025) off a COVID trough; underlying volume has been flat.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - lease principal - SBC - interest income), JPY m: FY2020 246,891; FY2021 26,811; FY2022 -69,533; FY2023 218,818; FY2024 124,169; FY2025 283,667. 3yr CAGR undefined (FY2022 negative). The series is dominated by working-capital swings (inventories +79bn release in FY2025, builds in FY2021-22), so the 5yr 2.8% is only indicative. EPS 5yr CAGR undefined (FY2020 loss, -16.5); FY2025 EPS includes a 70.4bn tax reversal (~53 yen/share post-split). All per-share figures post 2-for-1 split. JGAAP years (FY2019 and earlier) excluded from the CAGRs.

base.narrative: Implied EBIT margin (EBITDA - SBC - lease - D&A ex-ROU): 11.0% Y1 rising to 11.5% from Y4 -- the FY2026 guided 11.4% adjusted margin less a ~0.4pp recurring-restructuring allowance in Y1 (tariff step-up to 55bn, H2 FX normalisation), then flat. Growth: guidance +2% FY2026 off a TTM base already above it, then 2.5-3% price/mix-led, fading to 2% nominal JPY.

bull.narrative: Implied EBIT margin 11.4% Y1 to 13.0% by Y5 -- the 2024 mid-term-plan 13% target reached four years late and held, with higher growth capex (6.8%) to fund it.

bear.narrative: Implied EBIT margin 10.3% Y1 sliding to 9.5% by Y3 and staying there -- the FY2024 statutory level with restructuring that never stops; revenue -3% in Y1 on a stronger yen and OE decline, then ~1.5% nominal. Exit multiple capped at 12x for a de-rated cyclical.

scenario_narratives.base: Restructuring stage two is complete and its ~JPY147bn cumulative cost saving is real, but it is absorbed by the tariff step-up (JPY25bn to JPY55bn), low-end Chinese import pressure in Latin America/APAC and softer OE volumes, so the adjusted operating margin plateaus at the guided 11.4-11.5% rather than climbing to the 13% MBP target. HRD/premium mix and replacement-tire share gains deliver 2.5-3% nominal JPY revenue growth, fading to 2%. Capex (FY2026 plan JPY410bn incl. leases) runs ~0.5-0.7pp above D&A for Gen2 ENLITEN/MASTERCORE capacity before converging. Buybacks continue but are value-neutral in the model (flat count).
scenario_narratives.bull: Premium mix-up compounds: Europe gets to its 7%+ margin target, Truck & Bus and mining solutions keep lifting the Japan hub's 15.7% margin, Chinese TBR exit and the LatAm/EU plant closures prove to have removed the structural drag, tariffs are mitigated by local-for-local supply, and the yen stays weak. The adjusted operating margin reaches the 13% mid-term-plan level by 2030 and revenue grows 4-5% for three years. Still capped at a 15x exit multiple and discounted at the same 7.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Chinese and Korean capacity keeps moving up-tier (Sailun, Linglong, Zhongce) and into EV OE fitments, the US tariff hit of JPY55bn is only partly mitigated, a stronger yen (USD/JPY back toward 135) deflates reported revenue by 3% in year one, and a mining/freight downcycle hits the high-margin specialty tires. Management keeps restructuring (another plant-closure round) so statutory margins stay ~1pp below adjusted; the adjusted operating margin itself slips to the FY2024 statutory ~10% level. Terminal growth 1% and a 12x cap reflect a de-rated cyclical; net cash and the asset base keep the downside bounded.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the structural low-end competition that already forced the China TBR exit, the doubling tariff drag and the JPY translation exposure are all outside management's control and have no obvious end-date. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because the 13% margin needs several independent things to go right (mix, Europe recovery, tariff mitigation, weak yen, no mining downcycle) and the same target was already missed in the 2024 mid-term plan. Base 50%: guidance has been met or beaten for the last two years and H1 2026 ran ahead of the full-year plan.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Bridgestone is valued as a mature, net-cash, globally diversified cyclical whose intrinsic value is a stream of unlevered owner free cash flow built from components, not from the latest reported FCF. Three judgments carry the number. (1) The margin base is the company's adjusted operating profit LESS an allowance for restructuring that has recurred in every IFRS year (statutory operating margin averaged ~10.4% FY2021-25 against ~11.2% adjusted): the base case therefore holds the EBIT margin at 11.5% -- essentially the FY2026 guidance -- rather than assuming the restructuring tailwind compounds into the 13% mid-term-plan target (bull) or that the FY2022 pre-tariff 11.7% peak is a floor. (2) Leases are charged once, as an operating cost (treatment B), with lease liabilities kept out of net debt and D&A ex right-of-use used for the tax EBIT, which makes the IFRS-16 EBITDA comparable to the pre-IFRS era and avoids the double-charge seen on other Japanese filers. (3) Risk is charged once: one JPY-built 7.5% WACC for all scenarios, with cyclicality, tariffs and Chinese competition expressed in the scenario flows and in a 25/50/25 weighting rather than in an ad-hoc discount-rate premium. The terminal value is capped at 15x FCF (12x in the bear case), which binds in every scenario at a 7.5% WACC, so the valuation does not depend on the Gordon growth assumption. Buybacks are treated as value-neutral (they fund the flat share count); the real shareholder-return lever is the dividend, which is inside the FCF. FY0 is the TTM to June 2026 so that the flows and the June-2026 balance sheet (net cash JPY232bn, 1,244.6m post-split shares) carry the same date. Because SBC is 0.03% of revenue the house/street band collapses to a point and band_position is null.
valuation_philosophy.restructuring_margin_trajectory: Adjusted OP margin: FY2022 11.7%, FY2023 11.1%, FY2024 10.9%, FY2025 11.1%, TTM Jun-2026 11.65%, FY2026 guidance 11.4%. The recovery from FY2024 is treated as a return to the FY2022-25 range, not a new regime: the base case plateaus at 11.5% EBIT (11.0% in year 1 to absorb the JPY30bn tariff step-up and H2 FX normalisation), the bull case reaches 13.0% only in year 5, and the bear case gives back the recovery to 9.5%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin plateau assumption: every 1pp of sustained EBIT margin is roughly JPY45bn of FCF, i.e. about 10% of the base value; the 13% MBP target would add that twice over, a slide to 9.5% removes it twice over
FX translation: 86% of revenue is non-JPY; a 10% yen appreciation cuts reported revenue and FCF by roughly 8-9% with no change in the underlying business
US tariffs guided at JPY55bn in FY2026 (0.9pp of margin) with mitigation dependent on supply-chain moves that take years
Structural low-end competition from Chinese/Korean makers moving up-tier and into EV OE fitments
Recurring 'non-recurring' restructuring: FY2024 43bn and FY2025 94bn of restructuring expense excluded from adjusted OP; the base case carries only a ~0.4pp allowance in year 1 and none thereafter
Working-capital swings (FY2025 inventory release of 79bn) make any single year's FCF an unreliable anchor; the model builds from EBIT, so the TTM FCF of 432bn is not the base
Terminal value is cap-bound at 15x (12x bear): a market that de-rates global tyre makers toward Michelin's 10-12x FCF would cut the base value by roughly 15%
